scope: Terminal-state expectations for a single position (A64-014.6): the two ways a side loses that a board alone can show — no pieces left, and no legal moves — and positions that are not terminal. Draws are absent by construction: every draw in draughts is a property of the game's history, not of the position, and belongs to A64-014.7.

terminal_positions.description: LIGHT is to move and has nothing on the board. The more specific of the two reasons, which is why it is checked first — a side with no pieces also has no moves.

English rules, so the king reaches one square. LIGHT's king is cornered on a1 by a man it cannot jump — b2 is takeable in principle and c3 behind it is occupied. Blocked in is a loss in draughts, not the stalemate draw of chess.
Both sides have pieces and the side to move has moves. The common case, asserted so that an evaluator which called everything terminal would fail here rather than somewhere subtle.

A lone king against a distant man, and h8 cannot be jumped because there is nowhere beyond it. Between A64-014.3 and A64-014.5 the generator refused this position outright, so an evaluator built then would have read the refusal — or an empty list — as a loss for a player with eleven moves.

What LIGHT playing c3xe5 leaves behind: DARK to move with nothing left. Terminal detection runs on the position a move produces, which is why the lifecycle evaluates after applying rather than before.
